question: According to researchers1, EudraVigilance contains some 13 million reports, although around 6.3 million are visible on the public portal. Half of all reports – covering all medicines and vaccines in total aggregate – are reportedly being withheld2.

According to an EU-Vigil investigation, out of the total of 3 819 vaccines and medicines in the EMA’s database, the 22 COVID-19 vaccines increase the risk of thrombosis with thrombocytopenia six hundred-fold and the risk of heavy menstrual bleeding by a factor of 153.

The researchers criticise the EMA’s silence on side effects, particularly those affecting the heart, the nervous system and the female menstrual cycle. A year ago, the EMA reportedly asked them to delete this data and research on COVID vaccines. 1.
Can the EMA confirm that half of the reports in the full EudraVigilance database are not visible when consulting the public portal? If so, why?
Has it checked whether the EU-Vigil platform contains the data from the EMA that is not visible when consulting EudraVigilance, and the risks calculated by these researchers?
With regard to the COVID-19 vaccine or other medicines, has the EMA entrusted pharmaceutical companies or private consultants with analysing pharmacovigilance safety signals?
